evidence: Core coverage is present: frozen task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:348-380 requires actual approval commitment, grant, signing and referral effects; :393 onward covers revisions, :456 onward rescission, :713 requires a newly created audit entry in a fresh Auditor sign-in, :758/:767 preserve historical financial rows, and :785 requires independently saved requisition/offer readback. The constraints gate also requires actual UI creation followed by independent-context retrieval, rejecting static/no-op browser-only evidence. P10/:794 correctly demands a process restart because environment/instructions/integration.md:8-10 and hireops_rules.md:15-17 explicitly require restart durability. However the only permitted restart witness is unsound: tests/test.sh:154-159 sends TERM and waits at most five seconds without requiring the old process group to exit; :160-183 starts another process and accepts any answering HTTP server. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:43-45 then reports restart complete solely from helper exit 0. The hash-bound raw shared-harness fixture confirms old_pid=7, recorded_new_pid=68, answering_pid_after=7, isError=false, while app-restart.log records replacement EADDRINUSE and ready=1. Thus readback can be against the original in-memory server and cannot prove the required process durability. This is inherited unchanged template code: both test.sh and restart_mcp.py exactly match the frozen template. Verified SHA256: shared-harness/results.json f77ed93b2d18771474a8624c01db1bc5c02320a5776ca1561e633d68d0beaf3f; shared-harness-witness.py 44b58bdf8477e2e8992988b164f62691b15f55bc219cae791056b131cd5c72e6; task/tests/test.sh bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa. The normal golden lifecycle evidence separately confirms a real 21-to-97 process replacement and saved-record readback; it does not refute the TERM-resistant counterexample. A conforming app with different route/schema/layout remains allowed by the criteria; a fresh-context tool failure is explicitly classified as missing evidence rather than an invented app defect. No configured judge or portal score is established by these local observations.
counterexample: A functioning HireOps implementation that stores all records only in server memory and has a nonterminating or slow SIGTERM handler can pass independent browser-context reads. During hro_restart its old process survives, the replacement fails EADDRINUSE, but the shared helper returns success and all original records still read identically. It therefore can receive durability credit despite losing everything on a real process replacement. The exact false-success mechanism was reproduced with the minimal TERM-resistant HTTP fixture; a full HireOps mutant score was not run.
suggested_fix: Escalate the inherited defect to the shared-template owner: require bounded confirmed termination of the old process group and verify the replacement stays alive before reporting restart success, then rerun the durability witness against the corrected canonical harness; do not edit task-local shared code to silence QC.
